title: Distribute Candies
notes:
Task: A sister receives exactly half of an even-sized candy array. Return the maximum number of distinct candy types she can receive.
Idea: The answer is the smaller of the number of distinct types and half the total candy count.
Invariant: The traversal, frequency map, or DP state summarizes the portion already processed.
Edge cases: candyType=[1,1,2,2,3,3] -> 3
code:
class Solution:
 def distributeCandies(self,candyType): return min(len(set(candyType)),len(candyType)//2)
complexity_reason: A hash set counts the distinct candy types.

import java.util.*;
class Solution { public int distributeCandies(int[] candyType){Set<Integer>s=new HashSet<>();for(int x:candyType)s.add(x);return Math.min(s.size(),candyType.length/2);} }
complexity_reason: A hash set counts the distinct candy types.

title: Shortest Unsorted Continuous Subarray
notes:
Task: Return the length of the shortest continuous subarray that, if sorted, makes the entire array sorted.
Idea: Find the first and last descending adjacent pairs, compute the minimum and maximum within that range, then extend the boundaries while outside values violate the range.
Invariant: The traversal, frequency map, or DP state summarizes the portion already processed.
Edge cases: nums=[2,6,4,8,10,9,15] -> 5
code:
class Solution:
 def findUnsortedSubarray(self,nums):
  n=len(nums);l=0
  while l<n-1 and nums[l]<=nums[l+1]:l+=1
  if l==n-1:return 0
  r=n-1
  while r>0 and nums[r-1]<=nums[r]:r-=1
  lo,hi=min(nums[l:r+1]),max(nums[l:r+1])
  while l>0 and nums[l-1]>lo:l-=1
  while r<n-1 and nums[r+1]<hi:r+=1
  return r-l+1
complexity_reason: A constant number of scans locate the unsorted interval and extend it using its minimum and maximum.

title: Longest Harmonious Subsequence
notes:

title: Range Addition II
notes:

Invariant: The traversal, frequency map, or DP state summarizes the portion already processed.
Edge cases: m=3, n=3, ops=[[2,2],[3,3]] -> 4
complexity_reason: Only the minimum row and column bounds across the q operations are needed.

title: Can Place Flowers
notes:
Task: Determine whether n new flowers can be planted in a flowerbed without placing flowers in adjacent plots.
Idea: Scan left to right and plant in an empty plot only when its immediate neighbors, if present, are empty.
Invariant: The traversal, frequency map, or DP state summarizes the portion already processed.
Edge cases: flowerbed=[1,0,0,0,1], n=1 -> true
complexity_reason: The greedy scan visits each plot once and modifies the flowerbed in place.
